panels.rationale: Light microscopy of a human kidney biopsy from a patient diagnosed with minimal change disease (article title and in-text: 'the diagnosis of MCD with severe acute tubular necrosis was made based on the biopsy results'). The panel shows a glomerulus with open capillary loops and no proliferative/necrotizing changes, matching the vocabulary finding of a normal-appearing glomerulus on light microscopy, the histologic hallmark supporting MCD. Tubulointerstitial acute tubular injury changes are described in the caption but only partially covered by the vocabulary (proposed findings).

panels.figure_caption: Light microscopy showed that glomeruli have open capillary loops with no evidence of cellular crescents, fibrinoid necrosis, or endocapillary hypercellularity. The tubulointerstitial compartment is marked by severe acute tubular injury, with tubular dilatation, epithelial simplification, cytoplasmic vacuolization, and nuclear reactive changes. There is mild interstitial edema and patchy inflammatory infiltrate.
in_text_mentions: icroscopy showed severe acute tubular injury with tubular dilatation, epithelial simplification, cytoplasmic vacuolization, nuclear reactive changes, mild interstitial edema, and mild interstitial fibrosis (Figure 1). Electron microscopy showed diffuse effacement of podocyte foot processes (Figure 2). Thus, the diagnosis of MCD with severe acute tubular necrosis was made based on the biopsy results. The patient was started on prednisone. At discharge, patient was instructed to stop using BC powder. The kidney function improved within six weeks of treatment institution and dialysis was stopped.

panels.rationale: Real patient kidney biopsy (H&E) from a case report of minimal change disease in a person living with HIV; the caption/in-text explicitly state the glomeruli are normal on light microscopy, a core light-microscopy finding of minimal change disease, with arrows labelling 'Normal glomeruli' and 'Tubular dilatation with injury'. The accompanying acute tubular injury is a superimposed/secondary change not specific to MCD, so it is placed in proposed_findings. Single-image figure, so treated as one panel.

There were no cystic appearances typical of HIVAN.
